transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Well, doctor, I'm here because... honestly, things have just been really off lately. Ever since my father-in-law moved in with us, I've just been... different. I find myself snapping at my wife over the smallest things around the house, which isn't like me. And I'm putting off all these jobs and paperwork that I used to stay right on top of. It's like I just can't seem to get my head quiet, you know? Even when I'm out in the workshop or trying to get some fishing in, I just can't relax.
Have you lost interest in activities you usually enjoy, like spending time with family, fishing, or working in the workshop?

No, I wouldn't say I've lost interest. I mean... I still want to do those things. I still go out to the workshop, and I still try to get out on the water. It's just, like I was saying, when I'm actually doing them, I just can't seem to relax. But the interest is definitely still there. I just don't get the same peace out of it right now.
Have you noticed feeling down or depressed most days, even if just for a little while?
No, I don't think so. I wouldn't say I feel depressed or down. It's more just... I'm on edge, you know? Like I'm wound up tight, but not sad.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, like work, family responsibilities, or other everyday issues, even when there isn't a clear reason to be concerned?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm not just... worrying about everything for no reason. It's not like that. It's really just tied to the situation at the house, with my father-in-law moving in. That's what has me so on edge. I don't really sit around worrying about other everyday stuff unless there's an actual reason to.
Have you noticed any physical changes, like trouble sleeping, feeling restless, or muscle tension, since your father-in-law moved in?

No, not really. I mean, my sleep is fine. I'm not tossing and turning or anything like that. And I don't feel physically restless or have tense muscles. It's really just that mental feeling of being on edge, like I said. But physically, I feel pretty normal.
Do you feel like you're able to control the stress or worry about your father-in-law moving in, or does it feel like it's taking over your thoughts more than you'd like?

I wouldn't say it's taking over my thoughts, exactly. I mean, I can still focus on other things when I need to. But... I definitely don't feel like I have control over the stress of it all. It's just always kind of there in the background, making me feel wound up. I can't just turn it off or stop feeling on edge about the whole situation.
How long has this feeling of being wound up and on edge been going on since your father-in-law moved in?
It's been about five months now. It started up pretty much shortly after he moved into our house, and I've just been feeling this way ever since.
Have you noticed any other stressors or difficulties outside of having your father-in-law move in that have been contributing to how you've been feeling?

No, not really. It's honestly just the situation with my father-in-law. Everything else in my life is pretty much the same as it's always been. I don't have any other big problems or anything else going on right now that would be causing this. It really just comes back to him living with us.
Have you experienced similar feelings of being on edge or wound up in the past, even when there wasn't a specific stressor like your father-in-law moving in?

No, not really. I mean... I've never been the type to just feel on edge for no reason. If there wasn't something specific going on to stress me out, I was always fine. So, no, I haven't really dealt with this kind of thing in the past out of nowhere.
Have you noticed any other situations in your life, even small ones, where you feel similarly wound up or on edge, even if they’re not directly related to your father-in-law living with you?

No, not really. It's... it's just this one thing. Like I said, everything else is fine. I don't get worked up at the grocery store or, you know, dealing with bills or anything like that. It's just... it's really just him being in the house. That's the only thing that makes me feel this way.

Would you say that your feeling of being on edge is confined mostly to times when you're at home or thinking about the situation with your father-in-law, or does it also show up in other places or situations, even when he's not around?

It's really just when I'm at home, or, you know, if I know I have to go home soon and deal with him. When I'm out of the house, like running errands or visiting a friend, I actually feel okay. I can relax a bit. But the second I pull into the driveway, or even just start thinking about what mood he's going to be in, that's when I get all wound up again. So yeah, it's definitely tied to him and being at the house.
Would you say that if your father-in-law were no longer living with you, you would likely feel back to your usual self?

I think so, yeah. But... well, the situation hasn't really ended yet. He's still living with us, and all the caregiving and the changes to the house are still just part of my daily life right now. So I haven't really had a stretch of time where things went back to normal afterward to know for sure. But I'd like to think I'd be back to my usual self if he wasn't here.
Would you say that your main reaction to having your father-in-law living with you is feeling anxious or nervous, more so than just being stressed or irritated?

I'm not really sure how to separate them, to be honest. It's... I mean, I definitely feel nervous about what mood he's going to be in or what's going to happen next, but I'm also just really irritated by the whole thing. It all just kind of blends together. I don't know if I could say one feeling is definitely stronger than the other.
Have you noticed any new situations lately—maybe even small ones—where you feel that same nervous or irritated feeling, even if they don’t involve your father-in-law or being at home?

No, not really. I haven't noticed it happening anywhere else. Like I said, when I'm out doing other things, I feel fine. The nervous and irritated feelings really only hit me when I'm at the house or thinking about having to deal with him. It hasn't started creeping into other parts of my life.
